sources.author: James S. Milne

statements_used: Theorem 4.3, printed p.70 / PDF p.72: every ideal class has an integral representative of norm at most (2/pi)*sqrt(D), which is <5,<6,<9 for D43,67,163. The corresponding small rational primes are inert; possible ideal norms1 and4 give principal ideals.

sources.author: John Voight
sources.title: Quaternion Algebras
statements_used: Theorem15.5.5 and Example15.5.7, printed p.241 / PDF p.261: for every prime p congruent3 mod4, B=(-p,-1) has discriminant p and O=Z[(1+i)/2]+Z[(1+i)/2]j is maximal. Applied separately to43,67,163.
Theorem25.1.1, printed p.403 / PDF p.423: inverse-projective-unit mass (D-1)/12. Principal stabilizer2 gives w=6/(D-1), and the ramified fine point weight is nu=12/(D^2-1).
Main Theorem 14.7.4, printed p.226: rational reduced norms of a definite rational quaternion algebra are all positive rationals; used to identify the global norm-character quotient.
Main Theorem 28.5.3, printed p.473: strong approximation for the norm-one group when S contains a split noncompact place; removes character-at-a-split-place constituents.

Propositions 41.3.1 and 41.3.6, printed pp.756-757: all-integral-ideal degree sigma(m), relatively prime multiplicativity and unramified prime-power recurrence. Principal scalars act trivially over Q and on projective markings.

sources.author: Pierre Deligne
sources.title: La conjecture de Weil. I
statements_used: Theorem 8.2, printed p.302 / PDF p.31: for a normalized primitive cuspidal modular form of weight k >= 2, arbitrary level N and character epsilon, the roots of T^2 - a_p T + epsilon(p)p^(k-1) have absolute value p^((k-1)/2) whenever p does not divide N. Applied at k=2 and trivial central character; old spaces at other primes have the same unramified roots.
Theorem 1.6, PDF p.5: purity for smooth projective varieties over finite fields, as used in the existing transfer proof.
sources.inspection_scope: Actual Theorem8.2 text rechecked in this continuation; the arbitrary-level, unramified weight-two root bound is used on the primitive constituents underlying all cusp spaces. The retained M19 review also visually inspected this page. Deep proof remains imported.
